newsitem.title: USA: USDA data seen neutral for cotton prices-analysts.
newsitem.headline: USDA data seen neutral for cotton prices-analysts.

text.p: Cotton analysts said USDA's July supply and demand report contained few surprises and the market is not likely to react dramatically to the data.
"This report is neutral and contains very little to influence the market," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc.
USDA put the 1997/98 crop at 18.0 million 480-lb bales in its July report, compared to 18.5 million bales in June.
Exports were seen at 7.1 million bales versus 7.3 million bales, and ending stocks at 3.95 million bales, unchanged from the last report.
World production fell to 86.91 million bales from the June estimate of 87.50 million bales, and ending stocks to 35.24 million bales from 35.31 million bales.
Global use also fell to 88.11 million bales from 88.50 million bales.
"It's not a white knuckle time now," Smith Barney analyst David Brandon said, adding that the report reflects the market's general consensus about the crop.
He said one potentially friendly aspect of the reprot was a reduction in China's crop to an estimated 17.0 million bales from 19.3 million bales this season.
"This reconfirms a dramatic shift from cot acres into grains," Brandon said, adding that the reduction could translate into brisk export business for the U.S.
